posts.caption: The week I spend in New York for #Goalkeepers2030 and the UN General Assembly is always a highlight of my year. Last week was no exception.
At #Goalkeepers2030, I spoke with Archbishop Vicenzo Paglia about how people and relationships must remain at the center of how we use AI.

We have an opportunity—and an obligation—to ensure that AI tools are designed to improve lives and reach the people who stand to benefit most, including farmers, teachers, and health workers.  

Progress doesn’t happen on its own. It happens because the world invests in and prioritizes it. If we can combine increased generosity with the smart use of AI, there’s no limit to the progress we can make.

There are around 7,000 languages spoken worldwide, yet most AI tools are still built primarily in English. The Gates Foundation is joining a coalition of organizations to help nearly 3.4 billion people whose languages are underrepresented in AI. Over the next five years, these services will provide access to them in their own language and voice. #goalkeepers2030
I’m excited to be in New York this week to keep the conversation around AI moving forward and to build on the incredible progress we’re making. #Goalkeepers2030
Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen founded Hilarity for Charity to make sure no one has to care for a loved one with Alzheimer’s alone.

AI could be a great equalizer, but only if it’s built to benefit the people who need it most. 

That’s why the Gates Foundation is committing $1 billion over the next two years to expand access to AI and the solutions, opportunities, and knowledge that are too often inaccessible for many around the world—in health clinics, in classrooms, and on farms. 

This year’s Goalkeepers Report focuses on the urgent actions needed to ensure AI narrows the gaps between the richest and poorest rather than widening them.

AI gives us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help more solutions reach the people who need them. But there are three things the world needs to get right first. Explore more in the 2026 Goalkeepers Report.
AI has huge potential for agriculture, especially in low-income countries—and Neema Mduma is helping lead the way with KilimoAI.
This invention may have saved more lives than anything else in history.

Still the best tennis partner I’ve ever had.​

Congratulations, @rogerfederer on your induction into the Tennis Hall of Fame.
If the world takes the right steps, #AI will be a force for good and leave everyone better off. Click the link in my bio to read the full memo.
